details:
CosmoSmriti: The Universe Never Forgets

Project Overview

CosmoSmriti is an interactive 3D digital museum that brings the forgotten stories of NASA's abandoned and inactive equipment on the Moon and Mars back to life. Inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten," our project transforms space history into an engaging exploration and learning experience, especially for children, students, and space enthusiasts.

What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

The journey begins through the eyes of a friendly, curious robot. Rather than selecting a destination from a traditional menu, users explore the universe through the robot's eyes, with each eye acting as a gateway to either the Moon or Mars.

After entering a planetary world, users can explore its 3D landscape, discover different mission eras, and find hidden "Unknown Memory" markers representing forgotten space equipment. Selecting an artifact opens an interactive museum experience where users can explore its history, purpose, mission background, and scientific significance.

Our platform includes several educational and interactive features:

  • Interactive 3D Worlds: Explore the lunar and Martian environments.
  • Artifact Museum: Discover the stories and details of NASA's abandoned equipment.
  • 3D Artifact View: Inspect digital models and explore their structures.
  • Story Mode: Learn the historical background of each artifact.
  • Explain Like I'm 10: Understand complex space science through simple explanations.
  • Scientific Explanation: Explore deeper technical and scientific information.
  • Did You Know?: Discover interesting facts through interactive flip cards.
  • Mission Timeline: Follow important events in space exploration history.
  • Then vs. Now: Compare artifacts and their conditions across different periods.
  • Real Mission Map: Connect artifacts with their documented mission locations.
  • Last Documented Signal: Explore recorded mission communications or updates where available.
  • NASA Evidence Center: Access credible NASA sources and references.
  • Cosmic Memory Passport: Collect digital stamps as users discover artifacts.
  • Memory Archive: Explore a collection of preserved space memories.
  • Artifact Detective: Identify space equipment by solving clues.
  • Cosmic Quiz: Test knowledge through interactive questions.
  • Mission Time Machine: Travel through different eras of space exploration.
  • About Section: Discover our mission, vision, project goals, and why preserving these stories matters.

What Benefits Does It Have?

CosmoSmriti makes space history more accessible and engaging by combining scientific information with visual exploration and interactive storytelling. It helps younger audiences understand complicated missions without feeling overwhelmed by technical language. It also encourages curiosity, independent exploration, critical thinking, and learning through discovery.

Instead of presenting abandoned equipment as forgotten objects, the platform connects each artifact with the mission, people, and scientific achievements behind it.

Intended Impact

Our primary goal is to preserve the historical and scientific significance of NASA's abandoned equipment and make these stories accessible to future generations. We want users to understand that even when a space mission ends or its equipment becomes inactive, its contribution to human exploration remains valuable.

Through CosmoSmriti, we hope to inspire children and students to develop an interest in astronomy, space science, engineering, and future exploration.

Tools and Technologies Used

Our team used AI-assisted tools and web technologies to turn our concept into an interactive digital experience.

  • ChatGPT: Ideation, project planning, prompt engineering, feature development, and refining the user experience.
  • Claude: Research assistance for NASA missions, space artifacts, historical backgrounds, and scientific information.
  • Lovable: AI-powered website development, interface creation, and implementation of interactive features.
  • ElevenLabs: AI-generated music for the project's presentation and cinematic atmosphere.
  • NASA Resources: Mission records, scientific references, images, and other relevant information used to support the educational content.
  • Hardware: Standard computers and laptops for development, testing, research, and content creation.

The website was developed through AI-assisted web development. The exact programming languages and frameworks can be identified from our project's GitHub repository.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our most distinctive idea is the robot-eye exploration concept. We turn a familiar, friendly robot into a gateway to two planetary worlds, making exploration feel personal and exciting.

We also transform traditional educational content into an adventure where users discover artifacts, collect passport stamps, solve clues, test their knowledge, and travel through mission history. By combining 3D exploration, storytelling, gamified learning, and scientific references, CosmoSmriti creates a different way to experience space history.

Factors Our Team Considered

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Using credible NASA references and avoiding unsupported historical or technical claims.
  • Accessibility: Making information understandable for children and non-experts.
  • User Engagement: Designing interactive experiences that encourage exploration rather than passive reading.
  • Educational Value: Combining simple explanations with deeper scientific information.
  • Visual Experience: Creating recognizable and distinct Moon and Mars environments.
  • Historical Preservation: Respecting the importance of every artifact and its contribution to space exploration.
  • Usability: Considering navigation, responsiveness, and ease of interaction across devices.

CosmoSmriti is built around one simple belief: equipment may be left behind, but the stories and achievements behind it should never be forgotten.

The Universe Never Forgets. Now, Neither Will We.
